category_title: Artistically-inclined students who adapt storytelling skills to technical 3D modeling
minimal_context: The student is working on adding interactive game assets and obstacles to their 'Wheels on Fire' game level in the 3D Animation and Gaming track.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Let's review your 'Wheels on Fire' game level. Your classmates mentioned there isn't much for players to do yet, so please start adding interactive game assets and obstacles.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: I've been focusing on the environment. Since my school is by Fisherman's Wharf, I go there a lot and know how it should look. I just finished recreating the Golden Gate Bridge.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: That looks fine, but what about the interactive parts of the game?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: Well, someone observed that my early renderings were too flat, so I've been using the lighting tools to include shadows from the bridge and bike to create a better 3D effect.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: You need to focus on the gameplay now. What obstacles are you going to add for the player?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: I know peers said there isn't much for players to do, but I am most proud of the landmarks in my game right now. Honestly, I just wish I had time to add more scenery, like a silhouette of the San Francisco skyline, instead of figuring out how to add cars or pedestrians.
